title: Residential Electricity Supply Customer Agreement: Rollover at Contract Expiry
content:
**Conversion.** When a fixed or time-of-use term on a Residential Electricity Supply agreement reaches its contract end date without a renewal election and without a pending cancellation, the agreement converts on the following day to the plan named as the rollover plan, with a term of 0 months and an empty contract end date. The day after the expired contract end date is recorded on the agreement as its plan change date.

**Rollover rate, notices compliant.** When both expiration notices were compliant, the rollover rate is the rollover rate stated in the final options notice.

**Rollover rate, notices late or missing.** When either notice was missing or not compliant, the expiring contract rate is held for the plan's rate-hold cycles, beginning with the first cycle after expiry, and the variable rate rules apply only after those cycles.

**Terms after rollover.** A rolled-over agreement carries the rollover plan's terms in full, including no early termination fee. A rollover is never treated as a new enrollment and earns no sign-up credit.

## Decision table

| Renewal election made | Cancellation pending at expiry | Both notices compliant | What follows the contract end date |
|---|---|---|---|
| no | no | yes | Rollover; billed at the rollover rate stated in the final options notice |
| no | no | no (either missing or non-compliant) | Rollover; expiring rate held for the rate-hold cycles, then variable pricing |
| yes | any | any | No rollover |
| no | yes | any | No rollover |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A Beacon Ridge Price Lock 12 agreement ends 2026-04-30 with no election and no cancellation. On 2026-05-01 it becomes a Beacon Ridge Monthly Variable agreement with no term and no contract end date, and 2026-05-01 is its plan change date. Had the final options notice been issued too late, the expiring rate would be held for the first 2 cycles after expiry before variable pricing begins.
